purpose: Serve the local bilingual UI and authenticated API, run durable application workers and audit, and host the initial restricted NextOps PostgreSQL service until the approved database split.

authorization.notes: The owner authorized this deployment dossier and accepted Phase 0. VM creation, installation, private network access, database initialization, and service changes still require a separate approved change window.

vm.guest_os: Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS proposed; exact image and maintained patch lock required
vm.placement_status: Capacity-based proposal only; no reservation or VM exists by evidence in this repository.
vm.deployment_order: 1 of the three NextOps VMs; complete the private ESXi/storage/network preflight before creation
preflight_requirements: Refresh DS-C free space and reconcile any already-created VM before subtracting capacity.
Confirm available CPU/RAM, reservations, contention, VM compatibility level, guest features, and ESXi swap placement.
Confirm backing-storage health/latency, thin-disk commitments, snapshot/consolidation space, and the approximately 900-GiB DS-C free-space target.
Confirm approved local DNS, time, TLS, administrator recovery, and independent backup routes.
Keep ESXi intact; do not install NextOps in the ESXi management shell.

capacity_rules: The 200-GiB VMDK includes OS, application, initial database, logs, artifacts, and guest swap; do not add these again to the datastore budget.
Do not proceed until the application/database partition layout, WAL growth, evidence retention, rollback copy, and restore staging fit with measured margin.
Retain the project 3-TB ceiling and approximately 900-GiB DS-C free-space target; refresh capacity at the change window.
Independent off-host backup is required; another path or VM on the same G10 is only staging.

service_order.service: required mounts and protected key access
service_order.readiness: All expected filesystems are mounted with correct ownership; missing mounts fail closed.
Local engine accepts only the designed roles; migrations and append/audit constraints pass.

service_order.service: serialized database migration and identity bootstrap
service_order.readiness: Expected schema version and recoverable administrator identity exist; no default password.
Authenticated health distinguishes database, AI, connector, and audit readiness without exposing secrets.
TLS, local assets, security headers, bilingual login, and bounded proxying pass.
A versioned off-host backup and isolated restore test are recorded before production acceptance.

commands.purpose: Confirm the actual guest OS, kernel, and virtualization environment without changing them.
commands.expected_result: Ubuntu release evidence and VMware virtualization are captured in the private change record.
commands.failure_rule: Stop if the OS, kernel support, or virtualization environment differs from the reviewed lock.

commands.command: lscpu && free -h && lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,SIZE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINTS,ROTA && findmnt && df -hT
commands.purpose: Capture guest-visible CPU, memory, block devices, mounts, and free space.
commands.expected_result: Resources and intended mount paths match the approved deployment record with sufficient measured margin.
commands.failure_rule: Stop on an unidentified disk, missing mount, unexpected existing data, memory pressure, or insufficient capacity.

commands.purpose: Verify trusted time state and identify port conflicts before services are installed.
commands.expected_result: The approved local time source is healthy and planned ports do not collide.
commands.failure_rule: Stop if time is untrusted, listeners are unexplained, or the output cannot be handled as private evidence.

commands.run_as: developer in an isolated checkout without operational credentials
commands.command: uv sync --extra dev --frozen && uv run --extra dev ruff check packages tests && uv run --extra dev mypy packages tests && uv run --extra dev pytest
commands.purpose: Validate the only currently implemented Stage 1A contracts/policy slice.
commands.expected_result: Frozen install, lint, strict types, and tests pass; this still does not produce a deployable application.
commands.failure_rule: Do not build or promote an application release from a failing checkout.

commands.purpose: Verify every imported release artifact against the approved checksum manifest.
commands.expected_result: All expected files verify and the release ID, signer/authenticity evidence, licenses, and checksums are recorded.
commands.failure_rule: Fail closed on a missing or mismatched listed artifact; separately compare the bundle inventory with the approved lock and reject unlisted files. Never download a replacement during runtime startup.

commands.purpose: Install the application, database roles/migrations, system units or Compose stack, and reverse proxy.
commands.expected_result: A reproducible clean offline install from pinned artifacts.
commands.failure_rule: Blocked: no application installer, FastAPI stack, migrations, UI build, Compose definition, or systemd units exist yet. Do not invent commands.

commands.purpose: Start dependency-ordered services and verify authenticated readiness.
commands.expected_result: PostgreSQL, migrations, API, worker, and Nginx become ready without Internet access or fixed sleeps.
commands.failure_rule: Blocked until reviewed service definitions and health contracts exist and pass clean-install tests.

commands.purpose: Return to a last-known-good application release and compatible database state.
commands.expected_result: The previous release serves verified local login and retains durable audit/state or restores them from tested backup.
commands.failure_rule: Blocked until migrations define backward compatibility or an isolated restore procedure; never roll binaries back across an incompatible schema blindly.

audit append success/failure, redaction, and durable request/evidence references
database connections, locks, WAL growth, backup age, and free space
TLS expiry, time health, authentication failures, and reverse-proxy errors

unexpected exposure, secret leak, or resource exhaustion

required_inputs.validation: Record target identity, operator, timestamp, command list, and sanitized output reference.

required_inputs.validation: Private vSphere/ESXi evidence captured during the change window and reconciled against the four-VM budget.

required_inputs.validation: Clean offline installation, dependency ordering, hardening, resource limits, and rollback pass for the selected profile.

required_inputs.validation: Reproducible build plus clean offline install and complete checksum/license inventory.

required_inputs.validation: Capacity model includes growth and rollback/restore margin; mount failure prevents dependent service startup.

required_inputs.validation: Real isolated PostgreSQL tests cover least privilege, constraints, idempotency, audit, backup, restore, and recovery.

required_inputs.description: Private addresses, names, ports, identities, certificates, routes, and allowlists for browser, AI, connectors, DNS/time, administration, and backup.
required_inputs.validation: Only intended flows succeed; Internet, direct targets, database, model, and gateway exposure fail closed.

required_inputs.description: Protected local secret and key delivery, unlock, rotation, revocation, redaction, and break-glass recovery.
required_inputs.validation: Fresh offline login and service restart work; no secret appears in Git, process arguments, browser, logs, audit, or model context.

required_inputs.description: Independent backup destination, access identity, encryption/recovery material, schedule, retention, and agreed RPO/RTO.
required_inputs.validation: Isolated offline restore demonstrates usable identity, database, audit, evidence, and release artifacts.

required_inputs.description: Expected concurrency, latency/error limits, retention, sustained-test duration, and low-space thresholds.
required_inputs.validation: Targets are approved before measurement and actual p50/p95/error/resource results are retained.

acceptance_gates.description: Fresh Persian and English local login works with correct organization/environment scope and revoked/cross-scope access is denied.
Real PostgreSQL migrations, roles, durable idempotent runs, leases, audit append restrictions, restart recovery, backup, and restore pass.
Only HTTPS is exposed to approved users; database, AI, gateway, telemetry administration, and direct target access are not public.
Cold start from durable local artifacts and a fresh browser login succeed while Internet is blocked; no CDN, registry, public DNS wait, or external identity dependency occurs.
Mandatory database/audit/AI/connector failures are reported honestly and general local functions remain available where their own dependencies are healthy.
Independent backup and isolated restore meet the approved RPO/RTO and preserve required audit/evidence without relying on the same G10.

known_limitations: The repository currently contains Stage 1A contracts/policy only; there is no deployable API, UI, database schema, worker, installer, Compose stack, or systemd unit.
The 200-GiB disk has no approved partition or growth allocation and must not be formatted from this dossier.
Exact internal ports, certificate identities, secret mechanism, database roles, backup target, and performance objectives are unresolved private/deployment inputs.
All services share one physical G10 failure domain; this VM is not high availability.
